RagShortTexts: In 374 AD, Burgundians governed from Oder & Upper Main River, under the paramount rule of Burgundian Chieftains.
The polity asserted sovereign legitimacy anchored in Burgundians dynastic heritage and royal assemblies.
Surrounded by shifting imperial and tribal pressures, the regime enforced loyalty through binding oaths and martial law.

Variants.Content: In 374 AD, the sovereign authority of Burgundians anchored itself within Oder & Upper Main River, confronting the accelerating tremors of Late Antiquity. Governed by Burgundian Chieftains, the state projected imperial legitimacy through dynastic lineage, military patronage, and strict codification of feudal oaths. Emphasizing institutional doctrine rooted in Burgundians heritage, the crown mobilized loyal retinues and aristocratic councils to repel external encroachment. Beneath ceremonial grandeur lay unceasing vigilance against shifting steppe incursions and frontier uprisings, compelling the leadership to bind provincial magnates to the throne through land redistribution and martial alliance, safeguarding royal continuity amid an era of continent-wide transition.

Chieftain's riders gather at dusk to clean their weapons and talk about the oath sworn at midwinter. When the war horns sound, each man buckles on his armor and rides to the banner that carries the chief's name. The old warriors promise the younger ones a share of the spoils, and the young men believe it because they want to.

The chieftains' council wants you to confirm the land grants made to the river families before the autumn assembly. Confirm the grants only after the river families pledge their men to the next campaign. Send the pledges by a trusted messenger and keep the copies in your own chest, since an open register will reveal the grants to the other chieftains.
